thread:
Maya: quick update — ran Proteus8b through our standard bring-up. int6 baseline looks good; int4 gives ~2.6x token cost reduction but we see regressions on long-form recall and some hallucination spikes on multi-hop QA. attaching quick numbers below.
Alex: can you paste the mini scorecard? curious how it looks on GTN tasks (precision at top k etc).
Maya: sure — small table (very rough):
```
variant | tokens/sec | cost/unit | avg-rouge | longform-f1
fp16     | 1.0x       | 1.00      | 0.78      | 0.74
int6     | 0.95x      | 0.60      | 0.77      | 0.72
int4     | 1.05x      | 0.38      | 0.74      | 0.63
```
Maya: cost numbers normalized to fp16. int4 reduces cost a lot but longform-f1 drops ~15% relative to fp16 on our GTN slice. latency p50 roughly similar, p95 increases ~12% on int4 for long contexts.
Kevin: p95 up 12% is concerning for products with strict tail SLOs. what's the KV cache hit difference?
Maya: KV cache hit rate drops ~3pts on int4 (we suspect tokenizer differences + small topk instability).
Jamie: ops question — any higher error/oom incidents in the int4 runs?
Maya: no OOMs, a handful of decode anomalies (partial outputs) in 0.2% of int4 samples, none in int6/fp16.
Sophia: from product POV — GTN cares about top-1 precision and hallucination. a 15% drop on longform is non-trivial. but cost savings are tempting for high-volume ephemeral chat.
Alex: proposal: roll int6 as default for GTN-critical routes, enable int4 for low-risk bulk endpoints behind a traffic split. canary at 5% then 20% if metrics hold (hallucination rate, longform-f1, token cost).
Kevin: technical caveat — need to add routing policy so int4 only used when seq_len <= 512 and KV cache warm. that should mitigate the p95 and KV-hit issues.
Maya: agreed. ops checklist:
- canary config (5%) for non-critical routes
- monitoring: longform-f1, hallucination rate, p95 latency, kv-hit
- auto-fallback to int6 if hallucination > 1.5x baseline or p95 > baseline+200ms
- run extended slice eval after 1M tokens
Jamie: I can add the alerts and dashboards (will tag you when done).
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-config -> eng-ml-caninary at 2025-08-14T17:00Z :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maya: one more note — qualitatively some prompts where users expect reasoning (multi-step) break on int4. recommend adding a prompt classifier to route those to int6. simple heuristic: prompt length>200 or contains 'explain'/'step' -> int6.
Sophia: works for product. if the prompt classifier is cheap, we can get most cost benefit without hurting GTN metrics.
Alex: decision for now: implement Kevin's seq_len guard + prompt classifier + 5% int4 canary for non-critical. re-evaluate after 1M tokens, if hallucination stable -> 20% then broader.
Maya: will draft the short playbook and post slice examples. thanks all :thumbsup:
